facts.statement: Soriatitan is known from a single species named S. golmayensis found in the Golmayo Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from one species, S. golmayensis, found in the Golmayo Formation.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Soriatitan was discovered in the Golmayo Formation in Soria province, Spain.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Soriatitan, S. golmayensis, was discovered in the Golmayo Formation (upper Hauterivian–lower Barremian) in Soria province, Spain.

facts.statement: Excavation of the Soriatitan specimen began in 2000 by a team of paleontologists from Soria province.
facts.quote: Excavation began in 2000 by a team of paleontologists from the province of Soria

facts.statement: Preparation of the Soriatitan fossils began in 2009 with assistance from the Dinópolis Foundation.
facts.quote: preparation began in 2009, aided by the Dinópolis Foundation.

facts.statement: Soriatitan is estimated to have been 43 to 46 feet long and weighed about 8 tons.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have been 43–46 feet long (13–14 meters) and had an estimated weight of about 8 tons.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Soriatitan in the family Brachiosauridae within the superfamily Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Cladistic analysis has identified the known material as belonging to Brachiosauridae within Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: Soriatitan shares anteriorly deflected anterior-middle caudal neural spines with Cedarosaurus, Tastavinsaurus, and Venenosaurus.
facts.quote: It has similar anteriorly deflected anterior–middle caudal neural spines to Cedarosaurus, Tastavinsaurus, and Venenosaurus

facts.statement: Soriatitan was an adult grazer with small 0.7-inch (18mm) teeth.
facts.quote: The specimen was an adult with small 0.7 inch (18mm) teeth that indicates it was, like all other sauropods, a grazer.

facts.statement: Fossilized plant remains suggest Soriatitan lived in a subtropical climate dominated by conifer trees, which were likely its main food source.
facts.quote: Fossilized remains of plants that lived at the same time as Soriatitan indicate that it lived in a subtropical climate in a landscape dominated by conifer trees, which would have been its main food source.

facts.statement: Soriatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 138 and 129 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivió a principios del período Cretácico, entre 138 a 129 millones de años, desde el Hauteriviense al Barremiense en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The known material of S. golmayensis consists of a tooth, three dorsal vertebrae with ribs, a partial sacrum, five caudal centra, two caudal vertebral spines, a chevron, a humerus, an ulna, a radius, two partial ilia, two ischia, a pubis fragment, and a partial femur.
facts.quote: El material conocido de S. golmayensis (MNS 2001/122) consiste de un diente, tres vértebras dorsales con costillas, un sacro parcial, cinco centros de vértebras caudales, dos espinas de vértebras caudales, un cheurón, un húmero, una ulna, un radio, dos iliones parciales, dos isquiones, un fragmento de pubis, y un fémur parcial.

facts.statement: Soriatitan is estimated to have reached a full size of 13 to 14 meters and a weight of nearly 8 tons.
facts.quote: Se estima su tamaño completo en 13-14 metros y con un peso de cerca de 8 toneladas.

facts.statement: The specimen was an adult herbivore with small teeth measuring only 18 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El espécimen era un animal adulto con pequeños dientes de apenas 18 milímetros de longitud los cuales indican que, como los demás saurópodos, era un herbívoro.

facts.statement: The only discovered specimen of Soriatitan was found in the Golmayo Formation, dated from the upper Hauterivian to lower Barremian, in Soria province, Spain.
facts.quote: El único espécimen descubierto de Soriatitan, S. golmayensis, fue encontrado en la Formación Golmayo, datada del Hauteriviense superior al Barremiense inferior, en la provincia de Soria en España.

facts.statement: The material was found in the Zorralbo 1 deposit located near the town of Golmayo.
facts.quote: El material se halló en el depósito Zorralbo 1 localizado en vecindades de la población de Golmayo.

facts.statement: Excavation was started in 2000 by a team of paleontologists from Soria province, and fossil preparation began in 2009 with help from the Dinópolis Foundation.
facts.quote: La excavación fue iniciada en 2000 por un equipo de paleontólogos de la provincia de Soria, y se inició la preparación de los restos en 2009, con ayuda de la Fundación Dinópolis.

facts.statement: Until its discovery, it was believed that brachiosaurids had gone extinct in Europe about 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Hasta su descubrimiento, se consideraba que los braquiosáuridos se habían extinto en Europa hace unos 130 millones de años.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses identified the bones as belonging to a titanosauriform member of the family Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Los análisis cladísticos han identificado que los huesos pertenecen a un titanosauriforme miembro de la familia Brachiosauridae.

facts.statement: Like Cedarosaurus, Tastavinsaurus, and Venenosaurus, Soriatitan had anterior-middle neural spines inclined forward and a proximodistally straight lateral margin between the proximal head and humerus shaft.
facts.quote: Al igual que Cedarosaurus, Tastavinsaurus y Venenosaurus tenía espinas neurales anterior-medias inclinadas hacia adelante, además de tener un margen lateral proximodistalmente recto entre la cabeza proximal y el eje del húmero, como ocurre en Cedarosaurus.

facts.statement: The time range for Soriatitan is the Hauterivian to Barremian, from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)
